verdict: Nike's revenue fell 8% to $12.4B as wholesale and direct sales both shrank during its turnaround reset, and net income fell 26% to $1.2B.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: down 100 basis points, mainly on discounts and inventory reserves

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — footwear fell 14% to $3.2B while apparel grew 1%.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: The smallest decline of the regions — footwear fell 5% and apparel was flat.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Chuck Taylor brand — sales fell as demand cooled.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global Brand Divisions licensing revenue, less corporate items such as currency-hedge results.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — down 5%.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Revenue shrank in the reset
takeaways.text: Revenue fell 8% to $12.4B: NIKE Direct dropped 13% to $5.0B as digital sales fell 21% on fewer promotions, and wholesale fell 3% to $6.9B. Every region declined; North America fell 8%.

takeaways.title: Discounts squeezed margins
takeaways.text: Gross margin narrowed 100 basis points to 43.6% on higher discounts and inventory reserves; inventories were flat at $8.0B. Demand creation spending rose 1% while operating overhead fell 5%.

takeaways.title: Profit fell by a quarter
takeaways.text: Net income fell 26% to $1.2B and EPS to $0.78 from $1.03. New CEO Elliott Hill, who took over in October, framed the quarter as the start of a turnaround built on sport and full-price selling.

otherDetail: $24M of net interest income, plus $8M of other income, net.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($13M) and Corporate (-$25M, mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.
